transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining, happy Wednesday. Quick roll call — Isha and Miguel from our side, and from Vireo?
[00:08] Anita Rao: Hi this is Anita, thanks Sophie. Tom here as well.
[00:12] Miguel Torres: great, quick agenda — align on onboarding runway, security checklist, and pilot scope.
[00:18] Tom Brenner: Quick context — we're migrating an existing intent-classifier into a conversational assistant for clinicians. Need low latency, PII safe, and on-prem-ish controls.
[00:26] Isha Patel: Got it. When you say "on-prem-ish" do you mean fully airgapped or VPC with private endpoints?
[00:31] Tom Brenner: More VPC/private endpoints first; airgap later maybe.
[00:34] Lina Gomez: Security: we need SOC2, SAML SSO, and KMS-backed encryption. Also audit logs retained 1 year.
[00:42] Devon Li: we can support that — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit log export. Note: HSM integration depends on provider but we have patterns.
[00:50] Anita Rao: timeline — we want an internal pilot in 3 weeks, a wider pilot in 8 weeks. Is that feasible?
[00:56] Sophie Park: feasible but need infra deep dive — Isha can run latency baselines and Devon will help with model sizing.
[01:03] Isha Patel: For the pilot what are your target SLOs?
[01:06] Rajiv Menon: We want p95 under 250ms for short prompts, and throughput to handle 200 concurrent clinicians during shift changes (burst to 2k qps for a minute).
[01:17] Isha Patel: 250ms p95 is tight for large context. We usually recommend quantized model variant + prefix/KV caching to get there. Also batching settings need to be tuned.
[01:25] Ellie Park: Are there cost estimates for dedicated pool vs hosted? We have a tight budget.
[01:29] Miguel Torres: We can run a Dedicated reserved eval or start hosted and switch to dedicated for high-throughput windows. Our Optimize team will provide batching/cost recommendations.
[01:38] Tom Brenner: Network — how does VPC peering work? Do we need static routes?
[01:42] Devon Li: Two options: (1) Redwood Private into your VPC via VPC peering / private link; shared control plane lives in our managed plane but data path stays in your VPC. (2) Full on-prem package that is deployed inside customer network (airgapped) — that option has longer lead time. For peering we exchange CIDR & route tables, and you open specific outbound ports.
[01:57] Lina Gomez: KMS — can we bring our keys?
[01:59] Isha Patel: Yes bring-your-own-key supported. If you need HSM-backed CMKs we can integrate with common KMS vendors; there are a few extra auth hoops.
[02:08] Sophie Park: I'll share the runbook with the network checklist — it's the one with step‑by‑step peering examples and CIDR templates.
[02:13] Anita Rao: Sounds good. Pilot dataset — we'll share a de-identified test corpus of clinician dialogues. Any privacy notes?
[02:19] Miguel Torres: De-id is ideal. Also we recommend synthetic augmentations so evals cover edge-cases. We'll provide an eval harness.
[02:26] Rajiv Menon: On rollouts, how do canaries and fallback work? If model degrades we want instant fallback to smaller model.
[02:31] Devon Li: Redwood supports route-based rollouts: canary percentage, automatic fallback to a compatible variant, and A/B. We can configure the control plane to failover. There was a doc link: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/rollouts — I'll paste exact link in follow up.
[02:46] Tom Brenner: Can you run a latency baseline with our prompt set?
[02:48] Isha Patel: Yes — Tom please share the prompt file and sample traffic pattern; we'll run bench on staging keys. Typical turnaround 3–5 business days.
[02:57] Sophie Park: Security docs — Lina we have SOC2 and dataflow diagrams; I'll attach them. Also can share compliance pack (ISO if needed).
[03:05] Lina Gomez: Please include retention config for audit logs. We might need an export to our SIEM.
[03:10] Miguel Torres: We can configure log export to your S3 endpoint and push via connector.
[03:14] Anita Rao: Budget question again — if we start hosted then move to dedicated, what's the delta?
[03:19] Miguel Torres: Hosted per-token pricing, predictable for small scale. Dedicated has committed monthly fee plus lower per-token at scale — we'll send a pricing snapshot. For your expected peak, dedicated likely becomes economical after sustained X tokens/day — we'll model that.
[03:32] Rajiv Menon: Any dependencies from our side to get staging up?
[03:35] Sophie Park: Yes: (1) provide CIDR and admin contact for peering, (2) generate staging API keys, (3) share prompt/test dataset. We'll list these in the runbook.
[03:43] Tom Brenner: Who will lead the infra deep dive?
[03:45] Devon Li: Isha and I will own the deep dive; propose next Wednesday 8/19 16:00 UTC.
[03:52] Anita Rao: Works for us.
[03:54] Sophie Park: Recap — send runbook + pricing (Sophie), schedule infra deep dive (Isha/Devon), provision staging keys (Tom), deliver SOC2/HSM docs (Lina). Next sync after the deep dive, we'll have bench numbers.
[04:06] Miguel Torres: Quick note — we sometimes see transcription label mismatches in the runbook, ignore typos in doc names.
[04:12] Anita Rao: Haha noted. One more question: do you have a recommended model quantization profile?
[04:16] Isha Patel: For clinical prompts we recommend 8-bit quant + per-layer FP16 for critical ops; we'll suggest a profile after initial bench.
[04:24] Rajiv Menon: ok thanks everyone.
[04:26] Sophie Park: Thank you — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[04:29] Ellie Park: Thanks all.
[04:31] Meeting ends.
